title: Warehouse voice assistant pilot — engagement outline & pricing
content:
Purpose and summary:

This doc captures the proposed scope, technical approach, success criteria, timeline, and a draft pricing model for a 10-week Warehouse Voice Assistant pilot with Acme Fulfillment (example). Goal: validate operator voice workflows for inbound receiving, putaway, and short-picks with sub-500ms median response latency and operational cost targets compatible with Dedicated or Private deployment.

Context and motivation:
- Customer has ~3 regional warehouses, wants to reduce paper/paperless friction for first-mile receiving and occasional hands-busy scenarios.
- Primary UX is short-turn voice prompts (status checks, item confirmation, guided putaway). ASR handled by vendor X; Redwood provides language understanding, slot extraction, short instruction generation, and micro-dialog management.
- Important constraints: no PII leaves customer network for the on-prem option; hosted pilot acceptable for initial testing but long-term they prefer Dedicated or Private.

Scope (what we will deliver in pilot):
1) 10-week engagement: discovery, integration, pilot deployment, validation, handoff.
2) Deliverables:
   - Integration adapter for customer WMS (API mapping + 2 sample flows).
   - Voice prompt templates and canonical slot maps (receiving, putaway, short-pick).
   - Redwood route config: model variant recommendations (latency vs cost), batching policy, KV cache config for device prefixes.
   - Deployment: hosted sandbox + optional Dedicated staging environment.
   - Monitoring dashboards (per-route latency, token costs, per-device success rate) and a light evaluation harness (10 test prompts per flow).
   - Knowledge transfer and runbook (ops playbook + rollback).

Assumptions and boundaries:
- ASR and TTS are provided/managed by customer or partner; Redwood consumes text in a structured event.
- WMS access via REST API; customer will provide a staging API key and sample payloads during week 1.
- Supporting up to 60 concurrent voice sessions during peak; average utterance length ~10 tokens (post-ASR cleaning).
- We will use a mid-sized open model (approx equivalent of 30B quantized) for intent/slot decoding in initial pilot; we may recommend smaller quantized variant during Dedicated run to reduce TCO.

Technical approach / architecture:
- Flow: ASR -> Redwood request (utterance + device_id + context) -> model intent + slot extraction -> Redwood adapter calls WMS -> action/confirmation text -> TTS
- Deployments considered:
   * Hosted sandbox: fastest onboarding to validate flows and UX.
   * Dedicated: single-tenant GPU pool with predictable latency for production-like testing.
   * Private (VPC): required if customer mandates all inference inside their network.
- Performance knobs we will instrument: batching windows, prefix KV caching for known device phrases, model variant routing (low-latency vs low-cost).
- Edge adapter: small intermediary service running near devices (Docker container) to batch short requests and perform retry/backoff. We will deliver a reference image and configuration.

Success criteria (pilot acceptance):
- Functional: 90% of scripted flows (receiving/putaway/short-pick) complete without manual fallback during test harness runs.
- Latency: median inference response <= 500ms end-to-end (Redwood processing only), P95 <= 1200ms.
- Cost target: average inference cost per utterance < $0.015 for production mix (note: pricing estimate below).
- Ops: monitoring shows < 2% error rate attributable to model misclassification across the evaluation set.

Week-by-week milestone plan (10 weeks):
- Week 0 (prep): kickoff, access, security review, test data exchange.
- Weeks 1–2: discovery, WMS integration adapter, voice template design, test harness scaffolding.
- Weeks 3–4: hosted sandbox deployment, initial model tuning, iterative UX tests with 5 operators.
- Weeks 5–6: performance tuning, Dedicated staging (optional), load testing to 60 concurrent sessions.
- Weeks 7–8: quantization experiments, batch/cache tuning, build dashboards and run final evaluation harness.
- Weeks 9–10: handoff, runbook, knowledge transfer, and closeout report with recommendations for production (Dedicated vs Private).

Team and roles (Redwood):
- Solutions eng lead (1): engagement lead, customer liaison.
- Integration engineer (1): WMS adapter, edge image.
- ML engineer (1): model tuning, quantization recommendations.
- SRE/DevOps (0.5): deploy pipelines, monitoring.
- Product analyst (0.5): eval harness and dashboard definitions.
- Optional: Customer success and SE for on-site workshops (day rate).

Draft pricing sketch (pilot):
- Fixed services (SOW) fee — $60,000 (covers scoping, integrations, 6 engineer-weeks split across roles above, docs, runbook).
- Hosting / infra (sandbox, 10 weeks) — hosted credits included in SOW up to 1M tokens or equivalent; additional tokens billed at hosted rates if exceeded.
- Dedicated staging (optional) — if customer requests dedicated GPU staging during weeks 5–6: one-time environment fee $8,000 + $2,500/week for reserved capacity (up to 2 GPUs).
- On-site workshop (optional) — $3,500/day plus travel (1–2 days recommended).
- Extension option: production readiness package (migration to Dedicated or Private, SLA setup, extended evals) — estimated $120k–$220k depending on Dedicated capacity and Private on-prem packaging.

Pricing rationale and levers:
- Most cost associated with engineering time to integrate with WMS and tuning models for noisy ASR transcripts.
- If the customer commits to Dedicated capacity for production, per-utterance inference cost will drop substantially (we will provide quantization profile + DB of observed token distribution).
- We will propose a consumption offset (e.g., a credit applied to the first 3 months of Dedicated fees if they convert from pilot to production within 90 days).

Security/compliance notes:
- For hosted sandbox, data will be treated as ephemeral test data and not retained beyond logs needed for debugging; customer will provide sanitized test records.
- For Dedicated or Private, we will provide KMS integration patterns and advise on HSM/KMS for keys.
- Minimum network controls: VPN/whitelist for WMS, mTLS between edge adapter and Redwood endpoints for Dedicated.

Open questions / risks (to resolve during week 0):
1) ASR vendor: will customer prefer us to integrate with their existing ASR or test with a recommended partner?
2) Normalized utterance size: we assumed ~10 tokens post-cleaning; need sample transcripts to validate cost estimates.
3) WMS rate limits and sandbox SLA — need access to staging endpoints.
4) Device fleet patch/update policy — edge adapter deployment constraints.

Deliverable acceptance and next steps:
- Acceptance will be based on the success criteria above and a short closeout demo with customer stakeholders.
- Next immediate steps after internal approval: circulate SOW to Acme procurement, schedule week 0 kickoff, and request staging API keys and a dataset of 200 sample ASR transcripts.

Notes from preliminary workshop (internal capture):
- Operators indicated preference for terser confirmations (one-word or two-word confirmations) which affects prompt design and reduces tokens per utterance.
- Customer is enthusiastic about Dedicated for production but wants a clear TCO comparison (we will produce a 12-month cost model if pilot moves forward).
- Request: include an accessibility check for non-native English speakers; we should include simple accent robustness tests in the evaluation harness.

Appendix: quick ROI sketch (qualitative)
- Expected gains: 6–12% throughput improvement on receiving lanes during pilot hours, 20–30% reduction in mis-picks for short-pick workflows that are voice-triggered.
- Break-even: if Dedicated reduces per-utterance cost by 60% and usage scales to >500k utterances/month, the production migration cost is recoverable in 3–6 months (detailed model to be provided in production proposal).

-- end --

Action items (owner):
- Marco: finalize SOW draft and pricing sheet for customer review (by 2025-01-17).
- Aisha: prepare evaluation harness template and sample test sets (by 2025-01-20).
- Derek: stub WMS adapter repo and request staging API details (by week 0 kickoff).

Comments: this is intentionally conservative on Dedicated capacity until we have transcript size and peak concurrency verified. If customer can share 7 days of production ASR logs (redacted), we can tighten the cost estimate and recommended model variant list.")
